questions.question: Match the following formulas in MS Excel 365 with their respective results. Formulas Results (a) =RIGHT("siessies",4) (i) iessie (b) =REPLACE("sies",3,2,"sies") (ii) sies (c) =CONCAT("es","sies","sies", "es") (iii) sisies (d) =MID("siessies",2,6) (iv) essiessieses
questions.questionHtml:
Match the following formulas in MS Excel 365 with their respective results.

Formulas

Results

(a)

 =RIGHT("siessies",4)

(i)

 iessie

(b)

 =REPLACE("sies",3,2,"sies")

(ii)

 sies

(c)

 =CONCAT("es","sies","sies", "es")

(iii)

 sisies

(d)

 =MID("siessies",2,6)

(iv)

 essiessieses
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2

Key Points

  • The formula =RIGHT("siessies",4) extracts the last 4 characters from the text "siessies", resulting in "sies". Hence, (a) matches (ii).
  • The formula =REPLACE("sies",3,2,"sies") replaces 2 characters starting from the 3rd position of "sies" with "sies". The result is "sisies". Hence, (b) matches (iii).
  • The formula =CONCAT("es","sies","sies","es") concatenates the strings "es", "sies", "sies", and "es". The result is "essiessieses". Hence, (c) matches (iv).
  • The formula =MID("siessies",2,6) extracts 6 characters starting from the 2nd position of "siessies". The result is "iessie". Hence, (d) matches (i).

Additional Information

  • To summarize the matches:
    • (a) = (ii)
    • (b) = (iii)
    • (c) = (iv)
    • (d) = (i)
  • Correct Answer: Option 2

questions.question: Which file format is the most reliable for sharing documents when it is crucial that the recipient sees the document exactly as intended, with consistent formatting and layout, regardless of their operating system or the software they use to open it?
questions.questionHtml: Which file format is the most reliable for sharing documents when it is crucial that the recipient sees the document exactly as intended, with consistent formatting and layout, regardless of their operating system or the software they use to open it?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is PDF.

Key Points

  • PDF (Portable Document Format) is a universally accepted file format that ensures the consistent display of documents across different devices, operating systems, and software.
  • PDF files preserve the original formatting, layout, fonts, and images as intended by the creator, making them ideal for sharing professional documents.
  • The format is widely supported by various platforms and applications, including free PDF viewers like Adobe Acrobat Reader.
  • PDFs are secure and can be password-protected or encrypted to prevent unauthorized access or editing.
  • They are commonly used for contracts, reports, resumes, brochures, and other documents where consistent formatting is critical.

Additional Information

  • Features of PDF:
    • Supports multimedia elements such as audio, video, and hyperlinks.
    • Allows annotations, comments, and electronic signatures for collaboration and approval processes.
    • Compatible with printing, maintaining high-quality output without altering the document’s structure.
  • Comparison with Other Formats:
    • .docx: While .docx files are editable and widely used, they may not retain consistent formatting across different software versions or devices.
    • .odt: OpenDocument Text files are suitable for open-source applications but lack universal compatibility and formatting consistency.
    • .exe: Executable files are not document formats and are used for running software programs, not sharing textual content.
  • Advantages of Using PDF:
    • Ensures the integrity and professionalism of shared documents.
    • Reduces compatibility issues, making it accessible to a wider audience.
    • Provides security features to protect sensitive information.
  • Important Points:
    • PDFs are not designed for direct editing; specialized software is required for modifications.
    • They are ideal for final versions of documents meant for distribution, presentation, or archiving.
    • File size optimization tools can be used to reduce the size of large PDFs for easier sharing.

questions.question: Where as a computer mouse moves over the table surface, the trackball is
questions.questionHtml: Where as a computer mouse moves over the table surface, the trackball is
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Stationary.

Key Points

  • A trackball is a pointing device consisting of a ball held by a socket, allowing the user to control the cursor by rotating the ball with their fingers or hand.
  • Unlike a computer mouse, the trackball remains stationary while the user moves the ball to control the pointer on the screen.
  • This stationary design helps in reducing the required desk space and is more suitable for constrained working areas.
  • Trackballs are especially helpful for people with repetitive strain injuries (RSI) as they minimize wrist and arm movement.
  • They are commonly used in specialized applications like CAD (computer-aided design), gaming, and industrial control systems.

Additional Information

  • Trackball vs Mouse:
    • A mouse requires physical movement across a flat surface to track motion, whereas a trackball is operated by rolling the ball, keeping the device stationary.
    • Trackballs are beneficial for users with limited desk space or mobility issues.
  • Types of Trackballs:
    • Thumb-operated: The ball is controlled using the thumb, while other fingers manage buttons.
    • Finger-operated: The ball is controlled using fingers, providing greater precision for detailed tasks.
  • Advantages of Trackballs:
    • More ergonomic design reduces wrist strain.
    • Does not require a flat surface, making it versatile in various working environments.
    • Offers high precision and control, useful for design and gaming applications.
  • Limitations of Trackballs:
    • May require a learning curve for users accustomed to traditional mice.
    • Less common in general consumer markets, often making them more expensive.

questions.question: Consider the following statements about computer memory: ROM is used to store the BIOS in a computer. EEPROM is a type of memory that can be electrically erased and reprogrammed. Flash memory is a type of volatile memory. Virtual memory increases the effective size of RAM using the hard disk. Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.questionHtml:
Consider the following statements about computer memory:

  1. ROM is used to store the BIOS in a computer.
  2. EEPROM is a type of memory that can be electrically erased and reprogrammed.
  3. Flash memory is a type of volatile memory.
  4. Virtual memory increases the effective size of RAM using the hard disk.

Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement 1: True — ROM stores BIOS.

Statement 2: True — EEPROM can be electrically erased and reprogrammed.

Statement 3: False — Flash memory is non-volatile, not volatile.

Statement 4: True — Virtual memory uses the hard disk to extend RAM.

questions.question: (BABA) 16 in hexadecimal is what in octal ?
questions.questionHtml: (BABA)<sub>16</sub> in hexadecimal is what in octal ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 135272.

Key PointsTo convert the hexadecimal number (BABA)₁₆ to its octal equivalent, follow these steps:

Step 1: Convert Hexadecimal to Binary

Each hexadecimal digit can be represented by 4 binary digits.

B in hexadecimal is 1011 in binary.

A in hexadecimal is 1010 in binary.

So, (BABA)₁₆ in binary is:
B   A   B   A
1011 1010 1011 1010
Combining these, we get:
1011101010111010
Step 2: Group Binary Digits into Sets of Three (for Octal Conversion)
Starting from the right, group the binary digits into sets of three. If there are not enough digits to make a set of three at the left end, pad with leading zeros.
001 011 101 010 111 010
Step 3: Convert Each Binary Group to Octal
Convert each 3-digit binary group to its octal equivalent:

001₂ = 1₈

011₂ = 3₈

101₂ = 5₈

010₂ = 2₈

111₂ = 7₈

010₂ = 2₈

Combining these, we get:
1 3 5 2 7 2
So, the octal equivalent is (135272)₈.

Step 4: Match with Given Options
The correct octal equivalent is 135272, which corresponds to option 3.

questions.question: Word by default, places a tab stop at every______ mark on the ruler.
questions.questionHtml: Word by default, places a tab stop at every______ mark on the ruler.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 0.5".

Key Points

  • Word automatically sets default tab stops at every 0.5 inch (half-inch) mark on the ruler. This means that when you press the Tab key within a document, the cursor will jump to the next 0.5-inch position on the horizontal ruler.
    • Default tab stops: These are the pre-set 0.5-inch tab stops that Word automatically creates.
    • Custom tab stops: You can create your own tab stops at specific positions on the ruler to achieve more precise alignment. To do this, click on the ruler where you want to place a new tab stop, or use the Tabs dialog box (found under the Home tab or Paragraph dialog box).
  • Types of tab stops: There are different types of tab stops available in Word, each serving a specific purpose:
    • Left tab stops: Align text to the left of the tab stop.
    • Center tab stops: Center text around the tab stop.
    • Right tab stops: Align text to the right of the tab stop.
    • Decimal tab stops: Align numbers by their decimal points.
    • Bar tab stops: Insert a vertical bar at the tab stop position.

questions.question: Which of the following are Windows XP desktop elements? i- Taskbar ii- Desktop Icons iii- Background and other Display Settings iv- Grand Unified Bootloader (GRUB) icon

Which of the following are Windows XP desktop elements?

i- Taskbar

ii- Desktop Icons

iii- Background and other Display Settings

iv- Grand Unified Bootloader (GRUB) icon
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4

Key Points

  • Windows XP desktop elements include:
    • Taskbar: It is located at the bottom of the desktop and displays open applications, the start menu, and system tray icons.
    • Desktop Icons: These are shortcuts to applications, files, and folders placed on the desktop for easy access.

Additional Information

  • The desktop serves as the main workspace, allowing users to organize files, folders, and application shortcuts.
  • The taskbar and desktop icons are integral parts of the user interface, facilitating easy navigation and management of applications.
  • Background and display settings allow users to personalize their environment to match their preferences.

questions.question: The core part of an operating system which is one of the first programs loaded on start-up and manages computer system resources is:
questions.questionHtml: The core part of an operating system which is one of the first programs loaded on start-up and manages computer system resources is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kernel.

Key Points

  • The first program loaded on start-up and manages computer system resources is Kernel.
  • A kernel is the central part of an operating system.
  • It manages the operations of the computer and the hardware, most notably memory and CPU time.
  • There are five types of kernels:
    • A microkernel, which only contains basic functionality
    • A monolithic kernel, which contains many device drivers
    • Hybrid Kernel
    • Exokernel
    • Microkernel

Additional Information

  • Resources under the Operating System control:
    • The processor.
    • Main memory.
    • Input/Output Device.
    • Secondary storage devices.
    • Communication devices and ports.

questions.question: Find out whether the given statements are true or false. (i) MS-Word table has not less than two rows. (ii) MS-Word table has not less than two columns.
questions.questionHtml:
Find out whether the given statements are true or false.

(i) MS-Word table has not less than two rows.

(ii) MS-Word table has not less than two columns.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is (i) False, (ii) False

Key PointsMS-Word, a component of the Microsoft Office suite, is a versatile word processing program that allows the creation and formatting of text documents. Among its many features is the ability to insert tables into documents. Tables in MS-Word are used to organize and present data efficiently, and they are highly customizable.

To address the statements provided:

  • (i) MS-Word table has not less than two rows.
    • ​This statement is considered false because MS-Word allows the creation of a table with even a single row.
    • When creating a table, users have the flexibility to specify the number of rows and columns according to their needs, including the option to create a table with only one row.
  • (ii) MS-Word table has not less than two columns.
    • This statement is also false for similar reasons. MS-Word permits the creation of tables with just one column if desired.
    • The table creation feature is designed to be flexible, accommodating a wide range of table structures from a single cell (1 row x 1 column) to complex grids with multiple rows and columns.

Therefore, both statements are false because MS-Word's table feature does not impose a minimum of two rows or two columns, allowing users to create tables with as few as one row or one column. This flexibility makes it easier for users to design documents that meet their specific formatting and data presentation needs.

The correct answer is 1) (i) False, (ii) False, based on the explanations provided above.

questions.question: When entering data into Excel, why is it better to keep one logical item in each cell rather than mixing multiple items in a single cell?
questions.questionHtml: When entering data into Excel, why is it better to keep one logical item in each cell rather than mixing multiple items in a single cell?

options.text: It reduces the number of rows available
options.html: It reduces the number of rows available

options.text: It makes sorting, filtering and analysis easier
options.html: It makes sorting, filtering and analysis easier

options.text: It prevents the workbook from opening
options.html: It prevents the workbook from opening

options.text: It stops printing of the sheet
options.html: It stops printing of the sheet

questions.solution:
The correct answer is - It makes sorting, filtering and analysis easier

Key Points

  • Data Atomicity
    • Keeping one logical item per cell (atomic data) ensures that each data point is unique and easily accessible by Excel functions.
    • It allows the Sort feature to arrange data accurately in alphabetical, numerical, or chronological order based on a specific attribute.
    • The Filter tool works most effectively when cells contain distinct values, allowing users to isolate specific records without manual searching.
    • Placing multiple items in a single cell complicates the use of Data Validation and increases the risk of data entry errors.

Additional Information

  • Data Analysis and Reporting
    • Pivot Tables require clean datasets where each column represents a single category or variable for effective summarization.
    • Mathematical functions like SUMIF, COUNTIF, and AVERAGE cannot process individual components within a mixed-data cell.
    • Separating items prevents the constant need for the Text to Columns tool or complex Flash Fill operations during data cleaning.
  • Lookup Functions
    • Functions like VLOOKUP, HLOOKUP, and XLOOKUP rely on exact matches within a cell to retrieve corresponding data.
    • Data organized with one item per cell ensures that relational data management remains consistent across different worksheets.

questions.question: In Windows 10/11, which shortcut key combination allows a user to cycle through apps on the Taskbar in the order they are pinned?
questions.questionHtml: In Windows 10/11, which shortcut key combination allows a user to cycle through apps on the Taskbar in the order they are pinned?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Windows Key + T.

Key Points

  • The Windows Key + T shortcut is used in Windows 10/11 to cycle through applications pinned on the Taskbar sequentially. This functionality enhances productivity by allowing users to easily navigate apps without using a mouse.
  • When you press Windows Key + T, the focus shifts to the first pinned app on the Taskbar. Subsequent presses move the focus to the next app in the sequence.
  • Once the desired app is highlighted, you can press Enter to open it or activate it if it is already running.
  • This shortcut is particularly useful for users who prefer keyboard navigation and want to avoid using a mouse to switch between pinned applications.
  • The functionality is different from Alt + Tab, which cycles through all open windows, not just the pinned Taskbar items.

Additional Information

  • Windows Key + Tab:
    • This shortcut opens the Task View, which displays all open windows and virtual desktops.
    • It allows users to manage virtual desktops or switch between open applications visually.
    • The Task View was introduced in Windows 10 to enhance multitasking capabilities.
  • Alt + Tab:
    • The Alt + Tab shortcut cycles through all open windows, including apps that are not pinned to the Taskbar.
    • It provides a quick way to switch between active tasks without using the mouse.
    • Pressing Alt while tapping Tab displays a visual preview of all open windows.
  • Ctrl + Alt + Tab:
    • This shortcut is similar to Alt + Tab, but the window selection remains active even after releasing the keys, allowing users to use arrow keys or the mouse to choose a window.
    • It is designed for users who prefer a slower-paced method for switching between applications.
  • Taskbar Navigation:
    • Using keyboard shortcuts for Taskbar navigation, such as Windows Key + T, improves efficiency for power users.
    • Other related shortcuts include Windows Key + Number, where the number corresponds to the position of the pinned app on the Taskbar (e.g., Windows Key + 1 opens the first pinned app).

Important Points

  • Windows Key + T is specifically designed for navigating pinned Taskbar items sequentially, making it distinct from other window-switching shortcuts.
  • Shortcuts like Alt + Tab and Ctrl + Alt + Tab are focused on all open windows rather than pinned Taskbar applications.
  • Understanding these keyboard shortcuts can significantly improve multitasking efficiency, especially for users who handle multiple applications simultaneously.
  • Keyboard navigation is particularly beneficial for individuals with accessibility needs or those working on devices without a mouse or touchpad.

questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT a wired broadband?
questions.questionHtml: Which one of the following is NOT a wired broadband?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Satellite.

Important Points

  • An artificial satellite is an object that people have made and launched into orbit using rockets.
  • Aryabhata was the first unmanned artificial Earth satellite indigenously built by India.
  • Hence Satellite is NOT wired broadband.

Additional Information

  • A dial-up connection uses a standard phone line and analog modem to access the Internet.
    • A dial-up connection is established when two or more communication devices use a public switched telephone network (PSTN) to connect to an Internet service provider (ISP).
  • A cable is a hardware device that allows your computer to communicate with an Internet service provider over a landline connection.
    • A cable modem is a device that modulates and demodulates an analog carrier signal to encode and decode digital information that is transmitted.
  • A digital subscriber line (DSL) is a technology that transports high-bandwidth data over a simple telephone line that is directly connected to a modem.
    • This allows for file-sharing, and the transmission of pictures and graphics, multimedia data, audio and video conferencing, and much more.
    • DSL uses the analog medium, which is reliable and prevents interruptions and heavy packet loss.
